title: Heterogeneous failsafe shedding strategies for multi-region inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: design and implement a set of complementary, heterogeneous load-shedding mechanisms that keep customer-facing LLM endpoints within SLOs during multi-region incidents while minimizing user-visible degradation. This ticket covers the policy design, runtime admission hooks, region-aware circuit logic, and graceful degradation modes for request handling across hosted and dedicated deployments.

Background: Recent multi-region anomalies showed that single-mode shedding (pure token or rate-based) either causes hard failures for high-priority tenants or wastes capacity by preemptively rejecting all medium-priority traffic. We need an orchestrated approach that: 1) respects per-tenant priority and SLO budgets, 2) enables region-aware failover without cascading overload, and 3) applies progressive fidelity degradation instead of blunt rejections where possible.

Deliverables:
- Policy spec for "heterogeneous failsafe" (priority lanes + staged degradation + per-region circuit windows).
- Admission controller prototype with: time-budget enforcement, soft preemption, and tenant-weighted probabilistic dropping.
- Region-aware circuit breaker that coordinates via shared SLO credits and avoids simultaneous cross-region failovers.
- Graceful degradation handlers: response trimming, compressed/partial output, low-fidelity model fallback, and opportunistic KV-cache reuse.
- Integration tests and chaos-runbook for multi-region failover scenarios.
- Telemetry dashboards showing per-tenant rejection/fallback rates, recovery latency, and SLO burn.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end prototype deployed to staging covering two regions and one dedicated cluster.
- Under synthetic overload, tail latency stays within SLO for P0 tenants while P2-P3 clients see graceful degraded responses instead of hard errors in >= 90% of requests.
- No single-region controller decision should cause >10% simultaneous circuit trips in the paired region within a 60s window.
- Metrics and alerts in Console for new shedding modes; runbook documented in the incident wiki.

Design notes and rationale:
- Heterogeneous stack: combine deterministic admission (priority token buckets) with probabilistic soft-drop for best-effort lanes so that we preserve capacity for high-priority requests while allowing some degraded throughput from mid-tier tenants.
- Progressive fidelity: prefer returning partial or compressed outputs (e.g., truncated generation with a short_summary flag) to returning 5xx. This preserves UX while lowering CPU/GPU cycles.
- Region-aware circuits: maintain lightweight shared state (SLO credits) per tenant across regions using an eventually-consistent counter. Breakers trip only when local and remote credits are both depleted or when network partition prevents safe redirection.
- KV-cache reuse: when a request falls back to a smaller model, consult KV cache prefixes and cached reprompts to salvage previously-computed tokens before re-executing.
- Safety: fail conservative for enterprise tenants with SLA; allow configurable tenant override flags for guaranteed minimum fidelity.

Open decisions:
- Implementation medium: extend existing admission controller vs. build separate runtime filter chain. Prefer extensible filter chain if latency overhead can be bounded to <1ms.
- Coordination bus: use existing control-plane pubsub or a lightweight gRPC mesh for SLO credit syncing. Tradeoff between consistency and operational complexity.

References and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RELIABILITY/Heterogeneous+Failsafe+Shedding (draft)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 (branch: eng/hetero-shed)
